topic: 科学与口语深入讨论 · Independent new scenario: a lecture questioning simple explanations of cooperation
grammarFocus: 间接问句；名词性从句；比较、原因和假设表达综合。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Cooperation Illusion: A Lecture on Why Working Together Is Harder Than It Looks
instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何雅思分数。请先通读文章，理解大意；然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、判断正误/未提及）。之后学习语法部分：先看中文讲解，再完成8道独立语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目答案均可在文中找到依据。
passage:
Good morning, everyone. Today I want to challenge a belief that many of us hold without question: the idea that cooperation is natural and simple. We often assume that if people just talk to each other, they will find a way to work together. But my research suggests that cooperation is actually fragile, and that it often fails for reasons we do not expect.

Let me start with a simple example. Imagine two farmers who share a water pipe. Each farmer wants enough water for his crops. If both take water responsibly, the pipe lasts for years. But if one farmer takes more than his share, the other may respond by taking even more, and soon the pipe is empty. This is what I call a 'cooperation trap'. The farmers are not stupid or evil; they are simply reacting to uncertainty. When we do not know what others will do, we tend to protect ourselves first.

Now, you might ask why people cannot simply agree on rules. The answer is that rules only work when everyone trusts that others will follow them. In a famous set of experiments, participants played a game where they could either share money or keep it. When players could see each other's choices, most shared. When choices were hidden, sharing dropped sharply. This shows that cooperation depends less on goodwill than on visibility. If we cannot see what others are doing, we assume the worst.

Another common assumption is that punishment solves the problem. We think that if we fine people who do not cooperate, they will start to cooperate. But punishment often backfires. In one study, groups that introduced fines for non-sharing ended up with less cooperation than groups that had no fines at all. Why? Because the fine changed the meaning of the act. Without a fine, sharing was a generous choice. With a fine, sharing became a transaction. People began to calculate rather than to trust.

So what does help? The evidence points to three conditions. First, people need to interact repeatedly. One-time encounters encourage selfishness because there is no future to protect. Second, people need to know that their reputation is at stake. When others can see your past behaviour, you are more likely to act fairly. Third, people need a sense of shared identity. When participants in experiments were told that they belonged to the same group, cooperation rose even when the group was defined randomly.

These findings have practical implications. If you are a manager, do not assume that your team will cooperate just because you have told them to. Instead, create repeated opportunities for them to work together, make their contributions visible, and build a sense of shared purpose. If you are designing an online platform, remember that anonymity reduces cooperation. If you are a teacher, do not punish group members for one person's failure; instead, reward the group's visible effort.

Let me end with a question. If cooperation is so fragile, why do we keep believing it is simple? Perhaps because the belief itself is comforting. It tells us that we do not need to design systems carefully. But the evidence suggests otherwise. Cooperation is not a natural state; it is an achievement. And like all achievements, it requires effort, structure, and a little humility.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main point about cooperation?
options: It is natural and simple.
It is fragile and often fails unexpectedly.
It only works when people are punished.
It is impossible without money.
answers: It is fragile and often fails unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: 演讲者开篇即挑战“合作自然简单”的看法，并指出合作实际上是脆弱的，常因意想不到的原因失败。
questions.evidence: But my research suggests that cooperation is actually fragile, and that it often fails for reasons we do not expect.

questions.prompt: In the farmers' example, what happens when one farmer takes more water than his share?
options: The other farmer takes even more water.
The pipe is repaired immediately.
They agree on new rules.
The government intervenes.
answers: The other farmer takes even more water.
questions.explanation: 文中明确说，如果一个农民多取水，另一个可能取更多，最终管道空了。
questions.evidence: But if one farmer takes more than his share, the other may respond by taking even more, and soon the pipe is empty.

questions.prompt: According to the lecture, what did the experiments show about sharing when choices were hidden?
options: Sharing increased.
Sharing stayed the same.
Sharing dropped sharply.
Sharing became generous.
questions.explanation: 文中说当选择被隐藏时，分享行为急剧下降。
questions.evidence: When choices were hidden, sharing dropped sharply.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about punishment?
options: It always increases cooperation.
It often backfires and reduces cooperation.
It is the best solution for groups.
It makes sharing a generous choice.
answers: It often backfires and reduces cooperation.
questions.explanation: 演讲者指出惩罚常常适得其反，引入罚款的组合作反而更少。
questions.evidence: But punishment often backfires. In one study, groups that introduced fines for non-sharing ended up with less cooperation than groups that had no fines at all.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the three conditions that help cooperation?
options: Repeated interaction
Reputation at stake
Shared identity
Financial fines
questions.explanation: 文中列出的三个条件是重复互动、声誉风险和共同身份；罚款是之前讨论的无效方法。
questions.evidence: The evidence points to three conditions. First, people need to interact repeatedly. One-time encounters encourage selfishness because there is no future to protect. Second, people need to know that their reputation is at stake. When others can see your past behaviour, you are more likely to act fairly. Third, people need a sense of shared identity.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: When choices were hidden, sharing dropped ______.
questions.explanation: 文中原句为“sharing dropped sharply”，因此填sharply。
questions.evidence: When choices were hidden, sharing dropped sharply.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Without a fine, sharing was a ______ choice.
questions.explanation: 文中说没有罚款时，分享是慷慨的选择。
questions.evidence: Without a fine, sharing was a generous choice.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The speaker says that cooperation is a natural state.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 演讲者明确说合作不是自然状态，而是一种成就。
questions.evidence: Cooperation is not a natural state; it is an achievement.

options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 文中分别对经理、平台设计者和教师提出了建议。
questions.evidence: If you are a manager, do not assume that your team will cooperate just because you have told them to. Instead, create repeated opportunities for them to work together, make their contributions visible, and build a sense of shared purpose. If you are designing an online platform, remember that anonymity reduces cooperation. If you are a teacher, do not punish group members for one person's failure; instead, reward the group's visible effort.

options: True

grammar.title: 间接问句、名词性从句与比较/原因/假设表达综合
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 间接问句：用陈述语序，如“why people cannot simply agree on rules”；2) 名词性从句：如“that cooperation is fragile”作宾语；3) 比较、原因和假设表达：如“less on goodwill than on visibility”“because there is no future to protect”“If we cannot see what others are doing, we assume the worst”。注意间接问句不用问号，语序为陈述句。
grammar.example: Now, you might ask why people cannot simply agree on rules.

options: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I live?
answers: She asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: 间接问句用陈述语序，且时态需与主句一致（过去时）。
questions.evidence: 间接问句规则：陈述语序，不用助动词倒装。

options: I don't know why is he angry.
I don't know why he is angry.
I don't know why does he angry.
I don't know why he angry is.
answers: I don't know why he is angry.
questions.explanation: 间接问句用陈述语序：why + 主语 + 动词。
questions.evidence: 间接问句规则：陈述语序。

options: The fact that she passed the exam surprised everyone.
The fact what she passed the exam surprised everyone.
The fact which she passed the exam surprised everyone.
The fact she passed the exam surprised everyone.
answers: The fact that she passed the exam surprised everyone.
questions.explanation: 名词性从句作同位语时用that引导，不能用what或which。
questions.evidence: 名词性从句：that引导陈述事实。

options: He is more taller than his brother.
He is taller than his brother.
He is more tall than his brother.
He is tallest than his brother.
answers: He is taller than his brother.
questions.explanation: 比较级用taller，不能加more，也不能用最高级。
questions.evidence: 比较表达：形容词比较级 + than。

options: Because it was raining, so we stayed inside.
Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
Because it was raining, we stayed inside so.
Because it was raining, that we stayed inside.
answers: Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
questions.explanation: because和so不能同时使用；原因状语从句用because即可。
questions.evidence: 原因表达：because引导从句，主句不再用so。

options: If I will have more time, I will help you.
If I have more time, I will help you.
If I had more time, I will help you.
If I have more time, I would help you.
answers: If I have more time, I will help you.
questions.explanation: 真实条件句：if从句用一般现在时，主句用will。
questions.evidence: 假设表达：if + 现在时，主句will。

options: She explained that why she was late.
She explained why she was late.
She explained that why was she late.
She explained why was she late.
answers: She explained why she was late.
questions.explanation: explain后可直接接间接问句，用陈述语序，不需要that。
questions.evidence: 间接问句：why + 主语 + 动词。

options: The more you practice, the better you become.
The more you practice, the best you become.
More you practice, better you become.
The most you practice, the better you become.
answers: The more you practice, the better you become.
questions.explanation: “the + 比较级, the + 比较级”表示“越……越……”。
questions.evidence: 比较表达：the more..., the better...。

part1: Do you think cooperation is easy or difficult? Why?
Have you ever worked in a group where someone did not cooperate? What happened?
What makes people trust each other in a team?
Do you prefer to work alone or with others? Why?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you had to cooperate with others to achieve something. You should say: what the task was, who you worked with, what problems you faced, and what you learned from the experience.
part3: Why do you think some people refuse to cooperate?
How can leaders encourage cooperation in a group?
Do you think punishment is a good way to make people cooperate? Why or why not?
What role does trust play in cooperation?
